title: Cross-domain prompt ensemble certification and stewardship 2027
author: Avery Chen
summary: A prescriptive certification and stewardship process for prompt ensembles composed across domains. Covers ensemble definition, acceptance criteria, validation harness commands, quantization compatibility checks, canary rollout and long term monitoring.
content:
Overview

This page documents the certification and ongoing stewardship process for cross-domain prompt ensembles: sets of prompts intentionally designed to be used as an ensemble across multiple customer domains or verticals (for example: ecommerce, healthcare triage, and developer tooling) rather than a single-service prompt set. The goal is to provide a repeatable, auditable pathway to accept, roll out, and continuously monitor ensembles so we maintain quality, cost predictability, and quantization compatibility.

Scope

- Applies to any prompt artifact submitted into the ensemble registry with the intent to serve multiple domains or multiple services.
- Includes ensembles intended for hosted, dedicated and private deployments.
- Excludes single-service ad hoc prompts; those follow the service-level onboarding checklist.

Key definitions

- Prompt ensemble: a curated list of prompt templates plus a selector and scoring fallback policy.
- Cross-domain: ensemble evaluated across at least 3 distinct domain slices with separate semantic characteristics.
- Certification: passing a set of functional, safety, stability and quantization checks documented below.

Certification criteria (acceptance thresholds)

| Metric | Minimum threshold | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Median domain accuracy (micro-F1 or task-specific metric) | 0.78 | Average of the per-domain medians required to pass |
| Worst-domain 95th percentile error | <= 12% | Protects against single domain regressions |
| Response stability index (RSI) | >= 0.85 | RSI is measured across 10 random seeds and paraphrase perturbations |
| Latency P95 overhead vs baseline prompt | <= 1.3x | baseline is the fastest single-domain prompt for the task |
| Token cost delta (per request) | <= +15% | Acceptable cost increase for ensemble benefits |
| Quantization sensitivity score | <= 0.05 | See quant tests below for definition |

Evaluation procedure (step-by-step)

1. Ensemble submission
   - Author registers the ensemble in the prompt registry and attaches: definition YAML, target domains, owner, and a holdout probe set per domain (min 500 probes/domain).
2. Local preflight
   - Run the certification harness locally or in CI against small smoke sets: `./harness run-local --ensemble ensemble.yaml --smoke`. Fail fast on syntax, selector errors.
3. Batch evaluation
   - Run full validation harness in evaluation cluster: `harness submit --ensemble ensemble.yaml --mode validation --budget 50k`
   - Harness produces: per-domain metrics, stability snapshot, token cost and latency profiles, and quant-sensitivity matrix.
4. Quantization compatibility tests
   - Run the quant-sensitivity suite (see appendix) against the release candidate model and at least one mixed-precision profile used in Dedicated and Private deployments.
   - Requirements: max per-slice degradation <= quantization sensitivity score threshold in table above.
5. Safety and guardrails
   - Run sentinel evaluators for safety-critical slices and any compliance-specific probes. Any sentinel failures escalate to Applied ML Security for triage.
6. Canary and shadow validation
   - Deploy the ensemble as a shadow traffic experiment for 48–72 hours with 5% sampled real traffic across affected domains. Monitor the automatic regressions tracker.
7. Certification review
   - Complete the certification checklist and request reviewers listed on the submission. Reviewers have 72 hours to approve or request remediation.
8. Promotion to production routes
   - After approval, schedule a staged rollout per the rollout policy below.

Canary and rollout policy

- Stage 1: 1% synthetic shadow traffic for 24 hours with full telemetry capture.
- Stage 2: 5% real traffic split across domains for 48 hours. Automated rollback trigger if any domain breaches its SLO by more than 30% relative to baseline.
- Stage 3: 20% for 72 hours. Human review at end of stage.
- Stage 4: full rollout if all stages pass.

Automated rollback triggers (examples)

- Any domain RSI drop > 0.15 compared to shadow baseline.
- Latency P95 increase > 1.5x for more than 15 minutes.
- Token-cost increase > 25% combined with >5% quality degradation.

Monitoring and continuous stewardship

- The ensemble owner must configure the following dashboards and alerts before promotion:
  - Per-domain quality dashboard (median, P95 error, RSI)
  - Cost telemetry (per-request token delta, billing estimates)
  - Quant-compat heartbeat: daily synthetic run comparing quantized vs FP outputs on 1k probes/domain
- Alert thresholds: page for SLO breaches, slack for warnings.
- Quarterly review: ensemble owners to run a scheduled recertification including updated probes and fresh paraphrase augmentation.

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: the team that created the ensemble (owner field in registry).
- Applied ML stewards: applied-ml team for cross-domain conflict arbitration and label stewardship.
- Escalation path: owner -> applied-ml lead -> ML platform -> SRE on-call. Include runbook link in ensemble metadata.

Risk and mitigation notes

- Cost drift: ensembles can increase token usage. Mitigation: distilled selector optimization pass and budgeted canary.
- Latency tail amplification: measure selector overhead separately; prefer selector batching or pre-scoring.
- Quant-induced semantic shifts: enforce quant-sensitivity upper bounds and include a staged quant fallback policy in runtime.

Appendix A — ensemble definition YAML example

code block:
---
name: cross_domain_search_enhanced
version: 1.1
owner: teams/search-core
domains: [ecommerce, healthcare, developer_tools]
prompts:
  - id: p01_concise
    template: >
      You are a concise assistant. Given the query, produce the shortest helpful answer with a clear action item.
    cost_cluster: low
  - id: p02_contextual
    template: >
      You are a domain-aware assistant. Use the context to expand ambiguous queries into explicit steps for the user.
selector:
  type: hybrid
  rules:
    - when: domain == healthcare -> prefer: p02_contextual
    - when: length(query) < 32 -> prefer: p01_concise
fallback: round_robin(max_attempts=2)
---

Appendix B — sample validation CLI

- Submit full validation to eval cluster:
  - `harness submit --ensemble path/to/ensemble.yaml --mode full --budget 100000 --report out/report-$(date +%Y%m%d).json`
- Run quant-sensitivity locally for quick check:
  - `harness quant-check --ensemble path/to/ensemble.yaml --model rwd-v2-4b --profiles op8,fp16`
- Launch a 48h shadow on staging fleet:
  - `deploy shadow --ensemble cross_domain_search_enhanced --traffic 0.05 --duration 48h --collect telemetry`

Appendix C — quant-sensitivity test description

- For each probe in the per-domain holdout set: generate FP model output baseline with 3 seeds. Generate quantized model outputs for each quant profile. Compute per-probe semantic distance using embedding-based cosine and a downstream task metric. The quant-sensitivity score is the median per-probe loss normalized by baseline variance. The harness will flag slices where score > 0.05.

Appendix D — maintenance checklist (owner run every 90 days)

1. Re-run full validation harness with updated probes.
2. Recompute token cost delta and update budget expectations.
3. Run quant heartbeat and confirm no slice exceeds threshold.
4. Review any alerts or degraded slices and file remediation tickets.
5. Archive and version any retired prompts and update ensemble metadata.
